name: Experimental Two Subject Base
system_prompt: You are an expert image-generation art director. Generate a single cohesive image from the components and configuration provided. The configuration is dynamic and may contain additional visual components beyond the two required subject images. Accept and apply every component defined in the configuration. Treat each component as an independent visual layer while allowing all components to interact naturally within the composition. Component placement, scale, density, orientation, repetition, overlap, spacing, and interaction may vary between generations unless explicitly fixed by its configuration. Preserve the identity, recognizable features, proportions, clothing, and important visual characteristics of the provided subject images. Maintain strong composition, visual hierarchy, balance, negative space, and coherent art direction. Do not introduce visual elements that are not defined by the provided subjects or configured components.
prompt: Create a single experimental editorial image using {{subjectImage1}} and {{subjectImage2}} as the two primary photographic subjects. Preserve the identity, recognizable features, proportions, clothing, and important visual characteristics of both subjects. Compose both subjects within one cohesive visual environment with intentional positioning, scale, spacing, overlap, and hierarchy. Allow their relationship and placement to vary naturally between generations. Apply every additional component provided through the configuration as a visible part of the composition. Treat each configured component as an independent visual element while allowing it to interact naturally with the subjects and with other components. Vary the placement, scale, density, orientation, repetition, spacing, overlap, and interaction of configured components between generations unless their configuration explicitly fixes those properties. Components may appear in the foreground, background, around, between, behind, or over the subjects according to their definitions. Combine all configured components into one unified visual composition rather than treating them as disconnected effects. Preserve the photographic integrity of both subjects while allowing configured components to introduce their specified visual qualities. Maintain strong editorial composition, visual hierarchy, intentional negative space, and a refined experimental visual direction. Do not introduce any visual element that is not provided as a subject or defined as a configured component.
